newsitem.title: USA: US retail sales up 0.1 pct in 1st week Sep - Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US retail sales up 0.1 pct in 1st week Sep - Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.1 percent in the first week of fiscal September versus August, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook retail sales index.

The index rose 5.3 percent when compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also rose 5.3 percent in the week ended September 7 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

Year-on-year sales growth in the first week of September was below the pace set in August, and would have been worse had not heavily weighted Wal-Mart reported above-plan business for the week, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst of Redbook Research.
"Generally, I would say, business was disappointing," Eilenberg said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

"It would not have looked as good for this past week if it were not for Wal-Mart, (which) had a good week in terms of sales. Most of the other companies we surveyed reported mediocre business," he added.
Eilenberg also noted retail sales were hampered by the storm that rocked the southern part of the East Coast.
"A lot of people were affected by (the storm), and you don't go shopping in situations like that."
